p:cNvPr.descr: A two-part structure illustrating the Hox gene clusters and their effects on development. Part a is an ovular structure that is gray at the top left and middle. To the right of the gray, there is a small purple segment labeled as lab, followed by a larger green one labeled pb, followed by a slightly smaller light green one labeled Ser, followed by a yellow segment labeled Antp, followed by an orange segment whose bottom curves right, labeled Ubx, followed by a large red segment the length of the others combined, labeled adb-A. At the tail end on the right is a brown segment labeled adb-b. The first three segments together are labeled as the head; the next three are labeled as the thorax; and the last two segments are labeled as the abdomen. Below these labels is a multicolored insect whose segments match up with the ovular structure above it. In addition to the various segments, the insect also has a large wing that starts from the yellow segment and moves up and right above the orange and red segments. In part b, there are five rectangular lines; the first one belongs to Drosophila, and the second through fifth ones belong to a human. The lines are light blue, but have colored segments dispersed across the rectangle’s length. The first rectangle, labeled as HOM-C, begins with a light purple segment labeled as lab, followed by a dark purple segment labeled as pb, followed by a green segment labeled as Dfd, followed by a light green segment labeled as Ser, followed by a yellow segment labeled as Antp, then an orange segment labeled as Ubx, a red segment labeled as adb-A, and a peach segment labeled as adb-B. In between the yellow and orange segments are two lines that indicate a splice in the line. Below this structure is a rectangle representing Hox-A in a human. There are 11 dark blue segments dispersed across the length of the line, labeled A1 – A7, then a gap, then A9 – A11, then another gap, then A13. Dashed lines from the colored segments on the Drosophila rectangle point down to the A segments on the Hox-A; lab points down to A1, pb points down to A2 and A3, Dfd points down to A4, Ser points down to A5, Antp points down to A6, and Ubr points down to A7. Adb-A points down to the line, but not to a segment, and adb-B points down to A9, A10, A11, the gap between A11 and A12, and A13. Below that is another rectangle with shaded dark blue segments, labeled B1 through B9. After B9, the rest of the rectangle is light blue. The entire length of the rectangle is labeled Hox-B. Below that is Hox-C, which is another light blue rectangle. From the middle left, the dark blue segments are labeled as C4, C5, and C6, then a gap, followed by C8, C9, C10, C11, C12, and C13. Below that is Hox-D, which is another light blue rectangle with dark blue segments. At the beginning is D1, then a gap, followed by D3 and D4, followed by a long gap, then D8, D9, D10, D11, D12, and D13.
